title: Lehigh Valley Indian Americans Celebrate Diwali at Saucon Valley High School
excerpt: The Indian American Association of Lehigh Valley held its annual Diwali celebration on October 10 in Hellertown, an open-to-all day of performances, food and community run by the volunteer non-profit founded in 1972.
body:
• The Indian American Association of Lehigh Valley (IAALV) held its Diwali 2026 celebration on Saturday, October 10, from 12 p.m. to 9 p.m.
  • The event took place at Saucon Valley High School, 2100 Polk Valley Road in Hellertown, Pennsylvania, with tickets priced from $9 to $26.
  • IAALV's programmes are open to the public - membership is not required to attend.
  • Founded in 1972, the all-volunteer non-profit has represented Indian Americans in the Lehigh Valley for more than five decades.

The Indian American Association of Lehigh Valley brought the Festival of Lights to Hellertown on Saturday, October 10, holding its annual Diwali celebration at Saucon Valley High School. The day-long event, running from noon to 9 p.m., offered performances, food and festivities reflecting the traditions of India, and was reported as a joyous gathering for families, friends and neighbours from across the Lehigh Valley.

A day of light, culture and community

Diwali, the Festival of Lights, marks the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil, and IAALV's celebration is built around sharing that message beyond the Indian American community. The association describes the event as open to all, and its invitation was extended to the wider public: come with family, bring friends and neighbours, and celebrate together. Tickets were priced between $9 and $26, keeping the school-based celebration within reach for families.

The programme followed the pattern the association has built over many years - cultural performances on stage, Indian food, and a social evening that doubles as one of the community's main annual reunions. For many second-generation families in the Valley, the IAALV Diwali is the one event in the year where children perform, grandparents meet old friends, and newcomers find the community for the first time.

Five decades of volunteer service

IAALV was founded in 1972 and is a non-profit run entirely by volunteers. Its stated motto is "We care for the community we live in," and it represents Indian Americans across the Lehigh Valley. Diwali is the flagship of a year-round calendar that also includes a Holi celebration, the popular Foods of India event - where home cooks and local restaurants serve Indian dishes - Republic Day observances, an India Day programme and an Independence Day flag hoisting.

That breadth matters. The association's events are deliberately public-facing: its programmes are open to non-members, and its stated goal is bringing the community together and helping the wider Lehigh Valley community it lives in. The Diwali celebration functions both as a cultural showcase and as a fundraiser that supports the association's community work through the year.

What comes next

With Diwali 2026 complete, IAALV's calendar turns to its winter and spring programmes, and the association encourages residents who enjoyed the celebration to join as members or support its work as volunteers and donors. Details of upcoming events are posted on the association's website, iaalv.org. For Lehigh Valley readers, the takeaway is simple: this is a standing annual fixture, open to everyone, and one of the easiest ways in the region to experience Diwali with the community that celebrates it.
